chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no guest who camps with a people except that his sustenance is in his lap.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about a guest's sustenance when visiting a home?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the theological principle that while hospitality is a social obligation, the guest's sustenance is divinely pre-ordained, relieving the host of anxiety regarding provision. This reflects the Shia emphasis on trusting in Allah's distribution of rizq (sustenance) while actively fulfilling the rights of the guest, a concept deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition of generosity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is none from a guest who camps with a people except that his sustenance is in his lap’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
There is no guest who comes to a people without his sustenance in his lap.’”
